sections.title: Player-facing description
sections.body: The Wandering Briar is a living wall with memory in its thorns, sheltering some people and punishing anyone who treats it like brush.

sections.title: Public role
sections.body: Make plants active without turning them into generic monster vines.

sections.title: Handout text
sections.body: A mile-long living briar wall that blocks routes, shelters Wanderer families, and moves faster when its thorns taste blood.

sections.title: GM truth
sections.body: No forced reveal. Let this entity disclose truth through scene context and player attention.

sections.title: GM handling
sections.body: Introduce with sensory texture, then make one discoverable clue or social choice visible.

Player Safe: Players can navigate, search, read customs, inspect hazards The Wandering Briar when it is present in the fiction.
Gm Only: Use the roll only when the player's method, stakes, and consequence are concrete.

No Roll Reveals: Surface read: A mile-long living briar wall that blocks routes, shelters Wanderer families, and moves faster when its thorns taste blood. Give obvious visible facts freely; roll for meaning, risk, leverage, cost, or a hidden angle.

A flat read of The Wandering Briar hides the cost, motive, or useful next step. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear...
Fear Spends: Reveal who benefits from the current situation. Make the cost personal without closing off player agency.
Condition Options: No official condition unless a hazard creates Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable
Search Loot: Search yields context first: spoor, warning marks, tool scratches, route signs, or local testimony unless a scene names treasure.

The Wandering Briar is a place that has learned to move: thorn walls, dragged doors, laundry, hidden hollows, and paths that are different the next time you look. The place breaks into usable table spaces: Thorn mouth: The entry looks like a plant trying to be a doorway. Dragged-room hollow: Old cart panels and doors create private pockets. Block2: A long briar mass shifts around paths, wagons, and hidden shelters. Leaves face the sound of blood before they face sunlight. The briar opens more easily for people who move like they belong. Fresh thorns grow near recent violence. Detail Green sap, iron tang, crushed leaves, and damp earth under a bitter floral edge. Block4: The place changes even if the PCs stand still. Local people, creatures, weather, signage, and ward behavior all keep moving around the scene. Cutting blindly can close the path. Blood or panic changes the briar's behavior. The wall can protect and trap in the same beat. The briar moves faster after one drop of blood. A path behind the party closes without sound. Let the place be funny through overconfident signage, awkward forms, stubborn local habits, and magic that refuses corporate language.
